text:
Brandon Montour is playing like a man who's been handed the keys in Seattle. He's averaging 24:12 a night and has 16 points in 20 games, already half of last season's 32 in 64. The Stanley Cup winner from Florida in 2024 is the Kraken's top-pair puck mover now.

Our numbers like the effort and doubt the pace. His point rate (1.98 per 60) is above his talent range, mostly because Seattle has scored 7.3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of luck that fades. His own finishing is normal. The real good news is relative: the Kraken's share of expected goals is 6.2 points better with him on than off, on a team that loses the chance battle most nights. He blocks shots (33) and sets teammates up at the 83rd percentile among defensemen in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, so this is a real step. Our range projects 44 to 65 points.
